tagline: A two-car cable ferry crosses the Cashie south of Windsor.
intro: North Carolina DOT includes the Edenton-Windsor Loop among its Coastal Plain scenic byways. The agency’s byways program highlights roads for their distinctive qualities and opportunities to experience the state’s history, geography and culture. Edenton faces Albemarle Sound; south of Windsor, the Sans Souci cable ferry carries two cars at a time across the Cashie River.

Water crossings have changed here: trains once traveled by ferry between Mackeys and Edenton. In 1910, the Norfolk Southern Railroad built a wooden railway trestle between them. Maintenance costs ended its use in the late 1980s, and it was dismantled. The Sans Souci crossing has operated in some form since at least the 1800s; the state transportation department took over in the 1930s.

Windsor is the Bertie County seat, established at Gray’s Landing. Mackeys lies on Albemarle Sound’s south side, while Pea Ridge is near the Albemarle Sound Bridge. Edenton occupies the north end of Edenton Bay. The Sans Souci crossing is on SR 1500 south of Windsor.

moments.title: Windsor
moments.text: Windsor took shape at a place already known as Gray’s Landing, becoming a town by an act of the Colonial Assembly in 1768. It is the seat of Bertie County. The courthouse was built in 1889, a brick Neoclassical building with a polygonal cupola above its gable roof. Its portico was enlarged and wings added in 1941, followed by a rear addition in 1974. The surrounding historic district includes residential, commercial and institutional buildings dating primarily from after the turn of the 20th century. It entered the National Register in 1982, encompassing 78 contributing buildings.
moments.notice: The courthouse’s polygonal cupola rises above a gable roof.

moments.title: Edenton
moments.text: Fifty-one women in Edenton, led by Penelope Barker, signed a petition in 1774 to boycott English tea and other products. The boycott supported the organizers of the Boston Tea Party. The action became known decades later as the Edenton Tea Party. London newspapers responded with etchings depicting the women as uncontrollable. The Barker House, Penelope Barker’s home, interprets colonial history as a house museum. Another waterfront building, the Cupola House, was built by Francis Corbin in 1758 and stands there today. The Cupola House became a National Historic Landmark in 1970.

moments.title: Sans Souci Ferry
moments.text: The Sans Souci ferry follows a steel cable stretched across the Cashie River. Normally submerged, the cable rises from the water as the boat moves, assisted by rollers on its side. The cable stays attached to the ferry and holds it on course in normal currents. Drivers on the opposite bank summon it with their vehicle horn. The crossing takes roughly five minutes and saves a drive of about 20 miles. The operator controls a diesel engine, but the boat has neither brakes nor an onboard steering device. Regional DOT offices administer these inland cable ferries separately from the coastal ferry system.
moments.notice: The ferry’s rollers lift its normally submerged guide cable as the boat crosses.

practical: Sans Souci Ferry: The ferry carries no more than two cars and does not operate in high water or storms. (checked 2026-10-11)
